correctness.rationale: The all-positive labeling forces S to be a noncrossing forest. For a prescribed positive subset A, A plus all polygon sides is connected and noncrossing, and its forest A extends to a spanning tree in that graph with no other diagonals. This proves the full trace statement. A dissection has an all-diagonal face only if there is a cycle; conversely a cycle of selected diagonals encloses faces none of which can contain an original boundary side, by strict convexity. At the root side the incident face has an ordered list of at least two other sides. A side contributes x if on the original boundary and zG if a selected diagonal with an attached child. In a child at least one such side must be an original boundary side, explaining precisely the subtraction in G. The uniqueness explanation at RESULT.md:67 is imprecise: a mixed list can contain only one original boundary side. The actual recursion uses at least one factor x per surviving list, and after replacing U with V in its right-hand side the difference is divisible by x(U−V). It maps x²-series to x²-series and is an x-adic contraction, so uniqueness and recursive existence hold. Fans attain n−3. At equality a triangulation's weak dual has a degree-three vertex exactly when there is an all-diagonal triangle; otherwise the dual is a path. For n≥5, counting marked ears of the larger polygon by deleting a chosen label and reinserting in one of four terminal-ear sides of the smaller dual path gives 2Z_n=4n Z_{n−1}/(n−1), with cyclic symmetry distributing choices equally among the n−1 sides. The base Z_4=2 gives the claimed coefficient.
